newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Apple Fields sells 44 pct D.Brands stake. [CORRECTED 2:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Apple Fields sells 44 pct D.Brands stake. [CORRECTED 2:35 GMT]

text.p: Apple Fields Ltd said on Tuesday it had sold its 21.3 million shares (43.85 percent) of Dairy Brands NZ to Parapine Timber NZ.
The sale price is 43 cents per share, or NZ$9.1 million.
The sale is subject to due diligence, shareholder approval and completition of a rights issue by Parapine.
Parapine said in a separate statement to the Stock Exchange that it had bought a total of 50.04 percent of Dairy Brands from Apple Fields and Stan Alexander, at a total cost of NZ$10.49 million.

Apple Fields said there was provision for it to negotiate put and call options in Parapine's favour for the Diary Brands shares held by T/A Pacific Select Investments, the holder of 34.7 percent of shares in Dairy Brands.
If the proposed options were exercised the agreement provided for a premium to Apple Fields of up to approximately three cents per share.

Chairman Murray Valentine said the sale price would represent a $6.5 million write down of Dairy Brands' share value in the Apple Fields accounts. This reflected the current depressed state for all agricultural shares.
However, the prime director for Apple Fields at this stage was the concentration of resources on the company's property development strategies and debt reduction.

Valentine said the sale was consistent with the company's change of direction announced earlier this year where Apple Fields is moving out of apple growing and refocusing as a property development company.
